name: Canva
tagline: Template-based design suite for social posts, docs, decks, and brand assets

pricing.notes: Official pricing varies by region; 2026 public pricing coverage lists Canva Pro around $18/month in USD markets, while local pages may show regional currency.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 GB cloud storage; free-content library; free video exports up to 480p; paid assets remain watermarked unless licensed.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 100 GB cloud storage and premium templates, assets, brand tools and AI features.
tiers.notes: Annual price is $120 per person per year.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 500 GB cloud storage; 20x the Free plan's AI allowance; Leonardo.Ai Essential, Flourish Presenter and team/marketing controls; no seat minimum.
tiers.notes: Canva confirms monthly and yearly billing, but the current public page did not expose a stable USD annual-effective amount.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom enterprise pricing with approximately 1–5 TB storage depending deployment; public price is not listed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 GB storage and free-content access; free video export is capped at 480p, while premium assets require licensing.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Business pricing varies by location and team size
pricing.hiddenCosts: Premium content can require a one-off licence or paid plan, and regional pricing/tax can differ. Canva Teams is no longer sold to new sign-ups; existing Teams customers keep legacy pricing.

verdictSummary: A prompt-to-template design generator is buildable, but Canva's value is templates, stock assets, collaboration, brand kits, print/export workflows, and distribution.
coreLoopDIY: Generate simple social graphics from templates, edit text/images on a canvas, export PNG/PDF, and save brand colors.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because design work is mostly choosing from a huge polished library and collaborating without breaking layouts.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Open-source design/prototyping platform; not a Canva clone, but real prior art for browser

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: The closest hosted swap for social graphics, short video, documents, and templates; its best brand automation is also paid.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the Adobe Express desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly models power the generative features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, libraries and brand assets live in Adobe's cloud; exports include image, PDF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Adobe Express has a smaller template, app and content ecosystem and is weaker for Canva-style documents, whiteboards and presentations.

alternatives.name: Canva Free
alternatives.desc: Canva without the convenient tollbooths: plenty of templates, docs, decks, and exports, but no Magic Resize or serious Brand Kit.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install Canva's desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Canva AI and Magic Studio provide generative tools; Canva does not publish a complete provider/model map for the free editor.
facts.dataFormat: Designs, uploads, folders and brand assets live in Canva's cloud; users export common image, PDF, presentation and video formats.
facts.gapVsPaid: Canva Free keeps premium assets, Magic Resize, background removal and serious Brand Kit controls behind the paid plan.

alternatives.name: Desygner Free
alternatives.desc: A surprisingly complete free suite for templates, PDFs, scheduling, and small-team brand work, capped at three collaborators.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.engines: Desygner's terms identify OpenAI-backed AI features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, fonts and brand assets live in Desygner's cloud; designs export as image or PDF files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Desygner's template library, editor polish and extension ecosystem are materially smaller than Canva's.

alternatives.name: VistaCreate Starter
alternatives.desc: A generous social-design tier with one brand kit and unlimited exports; weaker for documents and presentations.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads and the single Brand Kit live in VistaCreate's cloud; exports include image, GIF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: VistaCreate is strong for social assets but much weaker than Canva for documents, decks, whiteboards and app integrations.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Penpot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Everyone reaches for it because it is open source; it is a product-design tool, not a template factory for posts, docs, and decks.

notes: An honest kinda: easy to demo, hard to match asset library and workflows.
prompt:
Build me a small canvas design editor to replace Canva Pro. Requirements:

- A local web app: Fabric.js on a canvas element with vanilla JS, and a tiny
  Express server for saving and export. Script tags only, no build step.
- Canvas presets: Instagram post 1080x1080, story 1080x1920, X header
  1500x500, A4 poster, plus a custom-size dialog.
- Editing: text using my local fonts, image upload, rectangles and lines, a
  layer list with reorder, align-to-center helpers, and snap guides at the
  canvas center.
- A brand panel loaded from brand.json: my 4 colors and 2 fonts as one-click
  swatches.
- Every design serializes to designs/<name>.json and reopens exactly;
  duplicate-as-template is the template system. Ship 3 starter designs.
- Export PNG at 1x and 2x via Fabric's toDataURL, and PDF by printing the
  canvas page with Playwright.
- All files local, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: stock photos, AI image tools, and collaboration. The asset
  library is what the Pro fee buys, I bring my own images.
- README: how to add fonts and where designs live on disk.
